title: Rails, Route 66, and the interstate
text: In 1880, the railroad chose a low pass over the Continental Divide in McKinley County for its line from Albuquerque to Southern California. Gallup was founded the next year, in 1881. That line is still one of the BNSF Railway's main transcontinental routes, and Interstate 40 runs alongside it through Gallup. The interstate replaced Route 66, and its bypass around Gallup was finished in 1980.

s3.quote: The freeway enters Gallup 20 miles (32 km) later, paralleling the Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railway's southern transcontinental mainline. ... It is the direct replacement for the historic U.S. Highway 66 (US 66). ... Gallup (1980)
